tags.gist: Says the paper credits human involvement as one risk-reducing category, though its strong and weak forms differ exactly where failures occur.
Repeats that supervision, deferral, adjudication and checkpoints are not one homogeneous category and proposes a vocabulary to separate strong from weak forms.
Recommends sponsors characterize each claimed human-in-the-loop control by domain-match, independence, triggering and timing criteria.
Recommends a benchmarking sub-element disclosing and testing fail-open versus fail-closed behavior of escalation subsystems under fault conditions.
Recommends multi-turn scope-drift testing over cumulative conversation state as a gate separate from per-turn boundary tests.
Recommends a distinct safety element for resisting sycophantic validation of unsafe decisions a patient or caregiver proposes.
Recommends LLM adjudicators disclose model-family relationship, decoding mode and training lineage relative to the generating model.
Recommends a three-state output classification with mandatory deferral on unverifiable claims, scored as its own competency.
Recommends a premarket disclosure of where the verification gate sits, and whether partial output can reach users before verification.
Recommends persistent structured logging of safety decisions, beyond transcripts, as a precondition before any postmarket monitoring credit is given.
Recommends the same domain-match, independence, triggering and pre-action gating criteria for agentic oversight checkpoints.
Proposes expert-in-the-loop as four properties, domain-matched reviewer, structural independence, deterministic triggering and pre-delivery gating, for sponsors to document.
Wants the activity axis paired with an oversight-quality modifier, since all supervised action-taking now sits at one point regardless of review quality.
Reports a generative triage layer failing open on API timeouts; wants an S.1 sub-element testing escalation subsystems under fault conditions.
Confirms cumulative reassurance drift from its own testing and wants a drift check over whole-conversation state as a separate gate.
Describes devices affirming a caregiver's risky plan to stop therapy; wants a safety sub-element for sycophantic validation tested in user-initiated scenarios.
Says organizational independence is insufficient for LLM adjudicators; wants disclosure of vendor relationship, decoding mode and shared training lineage.
Wants claims classified as supported, contradicted or unverifiable, with prespecified deferral on unverifiable scored separately from accuracy.
Reports streamed draft text reaching users before verification; wants gate placement relative to display disclosed premarket, apart from benchmark metrics.
Says re-benchmarking, clinician review and supervisory agents all depend on persisted safety metadata, so structured logging should be a monitoring precondition.
Wants agentic checkpoints to meet expert-in-the-loop standards, with compliance meaning no action without an affirmative, logged, domain-matched review.
Finds the frameworks well-constructed but says human involvement as a mitigating factor needs the same evidentiary rigor as the AI system.
